terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. An open-air Hindu street shrine of the Erawan type: a stepped dark-granite base on four gold feet, a railed upper platform with a gilt key-fret lattice, eight carved teak elephants massed two to a side, a stone pedestal with a gilt cap carrying a seated four-faced gilded deity with a raised right hand and a trident, four gilded columns with bracket capitals, and a steep gilded concave-pyramid canopy with upturned corners and a ball finial. Eight brass offering trays sit on the lower step.

reasoning: The registry notes say the openness is the point: four columns, a canopy and an open platform, so the deity is visible from the street on every side. There are no walls to hide anything behind.
Three instanced sets -- four columns, eight elephants, eight trays -- carry most of the parts at three submissions, which is what keeps a prop with 30 discrete pieces at 7 draw calls.

The plate for this build was regenerated WITHOUT the marigold garlands the first plate had, on the owner's instruction (no flowers or anything organic), so the offerings are the elephants and the trays alone and the material budget covers granite, gilt, teak and brass.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The seated deity is a small organic form -- 1.3 m in a 6 m prop -- and needs a torso tube whose section changes from hips to shoulders to neck; everything else is boxes, lathes and spheres.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The far two sides repeat the visible two: the proxy is symmetric to 0.01 H on every band.
The deity's four faces are suggested by four brow lobes on one head; the plate resolves one face.
The rail lattice is a painted key-fret canvas on a thin panel, not pierced geometry: an open lattice at 3 cm bar width is below the resolvable band and every gap is a hole-gate cost.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 5.00 x 6.00 x 5.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=12 materials, <=12 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole shrine. The physics compound is the derivation's own eight layers: coverage 1.00, overshoot 0.056.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up, square in plan with the deity facing +X. The plate is a three-quarter view from front-right; the prop is four-fold symmetric apart from the figure's pose and the elephants' walking direction.

silhouette.description: A stepped square base, a railed block, four slender columns and a steep concave pyramid roof with lifted corners and a ball finial. Band table against the Meshy proxy: mean |delta width| 0.036, |delta depth| 0.035 of height. The one flagged band (1.8-2.4 m, +0.16) is the solid rail panel's AREA against the proxy's open lattice -- the rail sits where the plate puts it, at the block's edge -- and band 8 (+0.05) is the fascia and lifted corners entering the 4.8-5.4 band.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span -2.50..+2.50, set by the lower slab's proud top plate; y spans 0.00 (the four gold feet) to 6.00, the top of the ball finial (centre 5.86, radius 0.14). Every height was read off the plate at 132 px/m (object 794 px tall = 6 m) and every plan width off the Meshy proxy's band table: 4.7 m across at 0-0.6 m, 3.84 at 0.6-1.2, 3.46 at 1.2-1.8, 2.7 across the colonnade, 3.6 at the eaves and 1.5 at 4.8-5.4 -- a steep concave pyramid.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Meshy accepted this plate (meshy/v7/image-to-3d, fal, ultra mode, 16,000 target polycount). The proxy is the plan-width ruler; the plate is the height ruler and the material evidence.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED, but the prop is four-fold symmetric by construction and the proxy's band table reads width and depth equal on every band, so the hidden sides repeat the seen ones.

featureReviews.evidence: A 1.3 m seated gilded figure on the pedestal's gilt cushion: crossed legs with knee spheres, a torso tube from hips to a neck with shoulders wider than the waist, a head with four brow lobes and a tiered hair spire, the right forearm raised with an open hand, the left arm down to the knee holding a trident. Visible through the colonnade from az 60-120; the hero 45 frame puts the front column across it.
featureReviews.notes: The first emit read the station tube's format wrong ([x, y, z, r, r] where tubeAlong takes [z, cx, cy, rx, ry] along z) and put the torso outside the base as a flat capsule while a bell of head and spire sat on the pedestal; the torso is built upright then stood up with rotateX(-pi/2). A torso wider at the hips than the shoulders still read as a bell, so the stations were re-cut with the shoulders as the widest ring and the legs ellipsoid narrowed from 0.88 to 0.72 m. Robe, face and hands are not authored at 1.3 m.

featureReviews.evidence: Four gilded columns at +-1.30 with ringed shafts, square bases and bracket capitals under an eaves beam; a steep concave-pyramid canopy 3.56 m square at the eaves (4.35) rising to 5.70 with 0.28 m upturned corners, a fascia, corner balls and a ball finial to 6.00; nothing between the columns.
featureReviews.notes: The preamble's hipRoof samples eight points per ring and creased the faces, so the roof is a bespoke square pyramid sampled eight times per side over twelve rings. Its winding was wrong twice -- the fascia black, then the slopes black -- and settled by probing the built bundle's face normals under Node (slopes had face normals pointing DOWN) rather than by eye. Band table against the Meshy proxy: eaves 3.6 m (band 7), 1.5 m at 4.8-5.4 (band 8, +0.05 residual from the lifted corners), columns 2.7 m apart (bands 4-6 within 0.025).

featureReviews.evidence: A 1.3 m seated gilded figure on the pedestal's gilt cushion: crossed legs with knee spheres, a torso tube from hips to a neck with shoulders wider than the waist, a head with four brow lobes and a tiered hair spire, the right forearm raised with an open hand, the left arm down to the knee holding a trident. Visible through the colonnade from az 60-120; the hero 45 frame puts the front column across it.
featureReviews.notes: The first emit read the station tube's format wrong ([x, y, z, r, r] where tubeAlong takes [z, cx, cy, rx, ry] along z) and put the torso outside the base as a flat capsule while a bell of head and spire sat on the pedestal; the torso is built upright then stood up with rotateX(-pi/2). A torso wider at the hips than the shoulders still read as a bell, so the stations were re-cut with the shoulders as the widest ring and the legs ellipsoid narrowed from 0.88 to 0.72 m. Robe, face and hands are not authored at 1.3 m.

featureReviews.evidence: Four gilded columns at +-1.30 with ringed shafts, square bases and bracket capitals under an eaves beam; a steep concave-pyramid canopy 3.56 m square at the eaves (4.35) rising to 5.70 with 0.28 m upturned corners, a fascia, corner balls and a ball finial to 6.00; nothing between the columns.
featureReviews.notes: The preamble's hipRoof samples eight points per ring and creased the faces, so the roof is a bespoke square pyramid sampled eight times per side over twelve rings. Its winding was wrong twice -- the fascia black, then the slopes black -- and settled by probing the built bundle's face normals under Node (slopes had face normals pointing DOWN) rather than by eye. Band table against the Meshy proxy: eaves 3.6 m (band 7), 1.5 m at 4.8-5.4 (band 8, +0.05 residual from the lifted corners), columns 2.7 m apart (bands 4-6 within 0.025).

featureReviews.evidence: Eight carved teak elephants 0.56 m long -- body, head, trunk tube, ears, tusks, four legs, tail -- two per side on the platform floor walking anticlockwise, and eight brass trays on the lower step. No garlands, flowers or fabric anywhere.
featureReviews.notes: The first pass at 0.44 m in a dark #5A3220 read as brown crabs; enlarged to 0.56 x 0.40 m and lifted to #74401F (saturation 0.73, so the tone holds on chroma against the backdrop). The trunk tube had the same station-format bug as the deity and now runs forward and down. Eight instances of ~900 triangles are two thirds of the prop's triangle count and are what distinguishes this shrine from a plain pavilion, as the registry notes require.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials: veined granite (vein-toned material under a marble multiplier tile), gold leaf at #DCB04A with metalness 0.35, oiled teak, brass, and a white carrier for the rail's painted key-fret. Three post-construction canvases at 4 MB.
featureReviews.notes: The granite field ships near luma 95 against a measured 62 because a low-chroma grey at 62 sits on the backdrop's 58 and reads as holes on the back-lit frame; the veins carry the identity. The gilt's metalness is held to 0.35: a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1 - metalness) and the first render's gold was brown at 0.55. The rail lattice is a painted canvas because a multiplier can only darken -- gold over grey cannot be painted onto either existing material, hence the fifth.

Mean |delta| 0.078/0.076 -> 0.036/0.035.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass: lower slab re-cut to top out at 0.62 (proxy band 1), railed block 3.52/3.80 m square, columns moved to +-1.30 (bands 4-6), eaves 3.56 m at 4.35 and a steep concave pyramid (band 8 read 2.07 m at 4.8-5.4 against the proxy 1.46). Band table 0.078/0.076 -> 0.036/0.035.

STATION TUBE FORMAT. tubeAlong takes [z, cx, cy, rx, ry] along z; the deity torso and the elephant trunk were written [x, y, z, r, r], which put the torso outside the base as a flat gold capsule. Both are built along z and rotated into place.

ROOF REBUILT AS A BESPOKE SQUARE PYRAMID. hipRoof's eight-point rings creased the four faces; sqRoof samples eight points per side over twelve rings with a corner lift that dies by a third of the rise and by |u|^2.2 along the side. Winding settled by a Node probe of face normals after the fascia and then the slopes rendered black.

DEITY AND ELEPHANTS RE-CUT. Torso stations with the shoulders widest (a hip-widest tube read as a bell), legs 0.88 -> 0.72 m, knees added, head enlarged; elephants 0.44 -> 0.56 m and lifted from #5A3220 to #74401F.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91 on the regenerated plate (no organics). Silhouette 0.93 against the Meshy proxy (mean 0.036/0.035 of height, the one flagged band the solid rail panel against an open lattice); structure 0.91 with four components and three instanced sets; form 0.88, held back by a 1.3 m figure that carries pose and proportion but no face or robe; material 0.89 with three canvases. 13,920/16,000 triangles, 7/12 draw calls, 5/12 materials, 7/12 unique geometries, ~65 ms factory.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Four components and three repetition systems: 7 of 12 draw calls.

materials.note: Five materials of twelve; the lattice carrier is the fifth and exists only because a multiplier cannot paint gold over grey.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 13,920 of 16,000: the eight elephants at ~900 triangles each are two thirds of it, and they are the identity of the platform.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes and lathes, a bespoke square concave pyramid, spheres and one stood-up station tube for the figure.
Three InstancedMesh systems carry 20 of the prop's 30 discrete parts.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless as a sculpt material; three Canvas 2D tiles (512 px, ~65 ms, 4 MB) are bound after construction: marble on the granite, the key-fret on the rail carrier, a light wear mottle on the gilt. Under Node every material keeps its flat colour.

risks.description: The granite field renders near luma 95 against a measured 62.
risks.mitigation: A grey at 62 sits on the backdrop's 58 and the back-lit 180 frame renders it at 0.55 of painted value; the veins carry the identity and the lift is recorded on the material.

risks.description: The turntable gate flags the open bays between the columns as holes on every azimuth.
risks.mitigation: They ARE openings: a wall-less pavilion shows the backdrop through its bays in the plate too. Measured with scratch/_holecc.mjs -- the two largest components are ~104 x 86 px beside the deity, 65-72 px thick, and no granite or gilt face appears among them -- and the gate is run with --allow-holes on that evidence, the mosque-courtyard case.

risks.description: The deity is 1.3 m in a 6 m prop and is read through columns.
risks.mitigation: Reviewed at az 60 where the plate shows it; the hero 45 frame puts a column across it.

risks.description: Band 3 of the proxy table reads +0.16 wide.
risks.mitigation: The solid rail panel's area against the proxy's open lattice; the rail is where the plate puts it.
